title: Distributional Extrapolation for Interactions
abstract: arXiv:2608.19849v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Predicting combinatorial effects from limited-range observations is a fundamental challenge in many scientific domains, including drug discovery and hyperparameter optimization. We study combinatorial extrapolation, where training data consists of axis-aligned samples with only one active covariate, while test-time inputs involve multiple simultaneously active covariates. We introduce DExtrI, a method for extrapolating interaction effects beyond the support of the training data. We provide theoretical guarantees characterizing when such extrapolation is possible. Empirical results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that DExtrI successfully generalizes to unseen combinations of covariates. Our approach enables applications such as predicting previously untested drug combinations and improving the efficiency of hyperparameter optimization.

translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2608.19849v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：从有限范围观测中预测组合效应是许多科学领域的基本挑战，包括药物发现和超参数优化。我们研究了组合外推问题，其中训练数据由仅有一个活跃协变量的轴对齐样本组成，而测试时输入涉及多个同时活跃的协变量。我们引入了DExtrI，一种在训练数据支持之外外推交互效应的方法。我们提供了理论保证，表征了何时这种外推是可能的。在合成和真实世界数据集上的实证结果表明，DExtrI成功推广到未见过的协变量组合。我们的方法支持诸如预测未测试药物组合和提高超参数优化效率等应用。
tldr: 本文提出DExtrI方法，首次在理论上保证并实证验证了从轴对齐训练数据中外推组合交互效应的可行性，应用于药物组合预测和超参数优化。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces DExtrI, which provides theoretical guarantees and empirical validation for extrapolating interaction effects from axis-aligned training data, enabling applications in drug combination prediction and hyperparameter optimization.
